abstract: We experimentally investigate and compare distributed state-of-polarization sensing in support-tube hollow-core and standard single-mode fiber. Despite significantly weaker Rayleigh backscattering and reduced polarization sensitivity in hollow-core fiber, polarization perturbations remain observable and spatially localizable, demonstrating the feasibility of SOP-based distributed sensing in hollow-core fiber
